subtitle: Saturday's board moved on totals, not sides — and in two of three spots, the true price still disagrees with where the number landed.
title: The Total at Ohio State-Texas Rose 2 Points. The Price Says Fade It.

body: No. 1 Ohio State at No. 4 Texas is the game of the day, and Texas is -1.5 — the market openly cannot separate them.
The number worth arguing with is the total. It opened 47.5 and is 49.5, two points higher — but the over got cheaper making that climb, -115 to -110.
When a number rises while the price on that same side falls, the number has outrun the money that pushed it there.
That's a fade, not a follow.
free.beats: What beats it: two offenses this good turning a coin-flip game into a track meet, which is exactly what those two points of movement were betting on.

also.body: The total opened 51.5 and fell to 48.5, but the price moved with it — the over got seven cents more expensive (-108 to -115) while the under got seven cents cheaper (-112 to -105). Work out the true price on each side and the over still comes out ahead, 51.1% to 48.9%.

The total hasn't moved all week — 9 at the open, 9 now — and neither has the price, -105 over and -115 under since the market opened. Work out the true price anyway and the split isn't even: 51.1% under to 48.9% over.

price_headline: Three prices, and what the market's true number says about each.
price_tail: Saturday's board moved on totals, not sides — the price didn't always come along for the ride.

move.headline: UCF AT PITTSBURGH
move.sub: Four points added to the total overnight, with the price barely moving.
move.body: UCF at Pittsburgh opened at 51.5 and is now 55.5 — the largest total move anywhere on Saturday's board — while the over price crept just two cents, -108 to -110. A four-point move on a nearly frozen price usually means the number is catching up to something the market already knew, not chasing new money in real time. If the cause is public by kickoff — a change at quarterback, a wind report — it'll be visible before the 3:30 PM ET snap; if not, the honest read is that the number moved and the reason never surfaced.

number.body: Iowa State at Iowa carries the lowest total on Saturday's board, and it hasn't moved an inch all week — 41.5 at the open, 41.5 now. The under price has, though: -110 to -118. When a total is already at the floor, the market stops moving the number and starts moving the price instead.

market: Eight cents of under money on a total that never moved is the same signal as a two-point line move somewhere else — it's just showing up in the only place left for it to show up. When a number is capped, at the floor, at a round total, or anywhere the book won't cross, the price becomes the only place left to watch. Reading it is the same skill either way: which side just got more expensive to bet, and by how much.
